recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If the work group wants to revisit integer-specific exclusion under the current number comparison model, handle that as a new search-prefix clarification rather than as unfinished FHIR-17669 work.
issue_request: FHIR-17669 was a Published FHIR-core Search page change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking whether the sa (starts-after) and eb (ends-before) prefixes apply to decimals. The approved resolution was to clarify that they are not used with integer values but are used for decimals, because decimals are covered by the number search rules.
initial_application: Jira comments identify GH#7fc760dc06 and state that the issue was already applied under a different task. Commit 7fc760dc068ce480e3a0572501f7124876d4d9f3 changed source/search.html to add 'but are used for decimals' to the sa/eb sentence.
additional_context: The Search page was later refactored by broader search-prefix clarifications. The current prefix section applies prefixes to ordered parameter types including number, defines sa and eb boundary behavior, and the current number section lists sa and eb among comparison prefixes whose use suppresses decimal implicit precision. Adjacent FHIR-17668 and later FHIR-26311/FHIR-40319 refine decimal range and prefix wording without reversing the seed's decimal applicability conclusion. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-17669 found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source file was changed. The current Search source already conveys the resolved behavior in the current terminology and adding the old exact sentence would be redundant and could conflict with the newer boundary-comparison presentation.
